title: Roadmap Ekoa: produção + concurso
intro: Regra de ouro: tudo o que está neste roadmap é feito no ekoa-code (versão nova). Nada é feito no ekoa dev (versão antiga). Zero novas features, zero correções na antiga, exceto emergência de cliente. Cada coisa feita na antiga cria nova divergência, invalida testes já feitos no novo e adia a produção.

items.text: Correr a bateria de testes automatizados completa no ekoa-code (pode ser hoje).
Correr um drill completo (Garrison) sobre o ekoa-code. Se o resultado do drill não satisfizer, registar as falhas e avançar na mesma: o drill não é gate desta fase.

Novo apanhado de divergências antigo→novo, para apanhar as alterações mais recentes feitas na versão antiga (correções de inserção de ficheiros, etc.). O apanhado anterior já migrou quase tudo; este é incremental.
Importar o artefacto do ERP Brasil Salomão do Ekoa de produção atual para o ekoa-code. Corrigir os problemas de importação que aparecerem.
Correr a bateria de testes existente do artefacto BSM (o projeto mais importante e único em produção) no ekoa-code. Corrigir até verde.
Pôr o agente a testar o ERP exaustivamente no novo.
Testar à mão o fluxo crítico: assinatura + SharePoint. Passar as integrações SharePoint e Outlook para o ekoa-code. (Nota de transcrição: "do ouro" interpretado como Outlook; confirmar.)

Passar pelas últimas demandas: relatório do Nicolas (tudo o que fez), email com as últimas demandas de coisas que não funcionavam, e pedidos anteriores. Dar ao agente a lista completa e verificar item a item que na versão nova está tudo a funcionar.
Produzir a checklist de go-live a partir de f0.1 a f0.8 e trabalhar sobre ela (formato checklist é o que funciona).
Go-live: ekoa-code em produção. A partir daqui, só se trabalha no novo.

categories.title: Workflows, Notifications and Channels (next feature line after Fase 0)

items.text: Phase 0, discovery (read-only). Verify the reuse map; report exists / partial / new per item; confirm the matter entity question (D4); confirm the WhatsApp Business platform constraints (6.5: approved templates outside the customer session window, a Business-platform number cannot also run in the regular WhatsApp app, per-conversation pricing); no building. Status 2026-09-03: the repository scan of the reuse map and of brief sections 3 to 9 is done and recorded in the note (verdicts, evidence and divergences); the D4 product decision and the WhatsApp platform check are still open, so this item stays open.

Phase 1, workflows core. Workflow entity and capability (Cortex, OpenAPI contract, user-or-key auth); manual trigger; the five step types (integration action, Ekoa action, agent step, gate, notify); change journal and undo per run; run summary; notifications entity and in-app area with badge. Build the notifications entity first inside this phase: Phase 2 depends on it. Acceptance: the Citius notification triage workflow (catalog 1) runs end to end on a real notification, pauses at the gate before the client message, resumes on the answer, and a run can be undone.

Phase 2, channels. Outbound delivery to WhatsApp and Slack with reply routing and audio; inbound CC email and WhatsApp with the media pipeline (transcription, OCR and vision, document parse); routing agent; auto-ingest with undo; document ingest (catalog 2) and voice debrief (catalog 3). Independent enough of Phase 1 to run in a parallel worktree (D10). Acceptance: a voice note sent to the Ekoa number updates a matter, and the lawyer answers a gate by replying "2" on WhatsApp.

Phase 3, listeners and cost. Event bus; listener triggers with model-evaluated natural-language filters; schedule as a trigger kind (D1); token accounting per run and per workflow; value receipts; global monthly ceiling for proactive runs (D2); enable/disable everywhere the workflow is shown; morning brief per matter (catalog 4) and deadline watch (catalog 7). Acceptance: the Citius triage workflow fires from the sync without manual action, and pausing at the ceiling is observable.

Phase 4, system workflows and creation. Workflows carried in packages; catalog with enable-and-configure (configuration questions declared by the workflow); conversational creation from the three entry points; in-conversation suggestion of repeatable requests; onboarding replaced by the package installer conversation; day-one reconstruction (catalog 14); cross-tenant learning ledger (metadata only, opt-out is D6). Acceptance: a new tenant completes onboarding in about five minutes and ends with enabled workflows and a practice picture.

Phase 5, client and lead workflows. Identity resolution of inbound senders by email or phone; remit and disclosure (D5); client status reply (catalog 5); lead intake (catalog 6); progressive autonomy exercised end to end. Acceptance: a client asks for status by email, the lawyer approves on WhatsApp, the client receives a disclosed reply, and after "always" the next one goes out without a gate and appears as done.

Phase 6, value library. Contract review against firm templates (catalog 8); legislative change to client outreach (catalog 9); hearing recording transcription for appeals (catalog 10); adversarial rehearsal (catalog 11); client audio explanation (catalog 12); quiet client reactivation (catalog 13); no-empty-screens rendering of run proposals inside the apps; firm brain and tenant style memory.

Open decisions D1 to D10: pending, owner Gonçalo (full text in the note). D1 schedule as a trigger kind through the Schedules entity; D2 default global monthly ceiling for proactive runs; D3 audio on notifications by default and TTS tiers; D4 shared matter/client entity before or alongside Phase 1; D5 exact PT-PT disclosure text; D6 tenant opt-out for the learning ledger; D7 gate ergonomics; D8 dedicated WhatsApp assistant number per tenant; D9 PT-PT UI vocabulary; D10 Phases 1 and 2 sequential or parallel.

Levantamento do que é tecnicamente possível: Citius (acesso de advogado com certificado; provavelmente automação de browser, sem API pública) e plataformas do notariado. Definir âmbito da v1: que atos, que consultas. (Nota de transcrição: "sítios" interpretado como Citius.)
Implementar a integração Citius v1.
Implementar a integração notariado v1.

Mecanismo genérico de códigos por SMS no Cortex: emissão, validação, expiração, rate limiting (por número, por IP), registo. Pensado como serviço reutilizável: logins, recuperação de password, verificação na webapp do concurso, futuro.
Primeiro caso de uso: Forgot Password no Ekoa com código SMS. Serve de validação do mecanismo em produção antes do concurso depender dele.
Escolher fornecedor (Twilio ou equivalente), configurar sender ID, custos.

categories.title: Fase 3: Tarefas como funcionalidade core do Ekoa

items.text: App de tarefas no Ekoa: um Kanban simples, ao estilo do que já existe no Garrison (portar o conceito, não reinventar).
Tarefas delegáveis a agentes: uma tarefa pode ser entregue ao agente para execução, não só gerida por humanos. É isto que torna "tarefas" core no Ekoa e não mais uma app de listas.

In ekoa, we should have a kind of billing area that shows sources of token usage. Sometimes it will be an app that is using tokens. Other times, it will be the knowledge research of sources that the user added. Other times, it will be the user actually building something or using the assistant.
Every time it spends tokens, it should create a registry entry of what it did and how many tokens were spent. If the user clicks, we should have a button or something near the token meter so that the user can click to see the details of what they are spending and how they are spending it, so that it's clear.
In some places in the app, we should show warnings that the user is about to spend tokens. For example:- In the settings, if the user enables test mode for all the artifacts, then they're spending tokens. They should receive a warning.- If they add a knowledge source that will be indexed every night and updated every night, they should be warned that that will happen and that they will spend tokens.

This should be a policy of a code that is not annoying. On the assistant, obviously, we don't need to tell the user that they're going to spend tokens. They know that if they're using artificial intelligence, they are spending tokens. Everywhere where it's not obvious, we should have it as a policy to always provide warnings to the user.
App Ekoa para o Omi (dispositivo wearable de IA): captura de gravações (reuniões presenciais, chamadas) e envio para o Ekoa.
Pipeline no Ekoa: transcrição → memórias, tarefas/ações (to-dos), tudo estruturado no sítio certo. O trabalho equivalente está em curso no Garrison; portar depois é fácil.
Instruções de utilizador: como adicionar a app Ekoa ao Omi, o que acontece a seguir. Página curta com link para o site do Omi a explicar o dispositivo.

categories.title: Fase 5: Bundles (venda de pacotes de aplicações)

items.text: Área de bundles dentro da aplicação Ekoa: escolher aplicações, ver demos, adicionar um bundle à conta.

Página de bundles no site do Ekoa. Regra de preços: nunca mostrar o preço do bundle sozinho. Mostrar sempre dois valores: preço do bundle para quem já é cliente Ekoa, e preço bundle + subscrição (subscrição corrente à data + valor do bundle).
Página de detalhe do bundle: é a mesma página com ou sem link de parceiro (reutilizar tudo). Sem link/código, não há atribuição de referral.
Link de parceiro com código → aterra direto no detalhe do bundle. A venda por esse link fica registada com atribuição ao parceiro.

Notificação de venda: numa fase inicial, o pagamento ao parceiro é manual; basta o Gonçalo ser notificado (email ou equivalente) de cada venda com atribuição, para pagar. Pagamentos automatizados ficam para mais tarde.
Definir a mecânica exata do código de referral (em aberto): quando é atribuído, se se pede código no checkout sem link, se o código só nasce depois da primeira venda.
Landing do concurso: o que é, prémios, regulamento, como participar. Instruções muito fáceis, passo a passo.

Criação de contas gratuitas únicas: a pessoa escreve a descrição da app que quer, carrega em "criar aplicação", verifica o número por SMS (mecanismo da Fase 2), e recebe uma conta Ekoa gerada (username aleatório + password aleatória), de preferência com link que entra já autenticado. Limite de utilização por tokens.
Fluxo de criação da app via API do Cortex: descrição → app gerada → ajustes iterativos, dentro dos limites (prompts e tokens), sem custo para a pessoa.

Submissão a votação: descrição da aplicação + link para a app a correr no Ekoa + preço pretendido de venda (não final, sujeito a aprovação do Ekoa). Instruções claras de como copiar o link da app e submeter.
Sistema de votação: um voto por número de telefone verificado por SMS.
Galeria pública das submissões com votação.
Backoffice mínimo: moderação de submissões (barra mínima de validade), monitorização de votos e de consumo de tokens, exportação de contactos.
Validar regulamento com advogado e contabilista.
Pré-comprometer 12 a 15 participantes antes de qualquer anúncio público (rede: Marília, Alexandra, BSM, Nicolas, Nicholas).
Anúncio e abertura. Fóruns e comunidades de advogados como canal principal: o desenho é comunidade a descobrir, criar, experimentar as apps uns dos outros e votar.
Acompanhamento: consumo de tokens, fraude de votos, qualidade das submissões.
Encerramento, apuramento, entrega de prémios, imprensa, casos de estudo.

funds app - I want to create an app on ekoa for working with public funds and European funds, support for companies, big and small, but not for small companies, and maybe even for individuals as well. This includes hiring support from the IEFB, the PRR funds, European funds, and other kinds of support that we can add to the basic sources of knowledge of ekoa.  The app is able to guide the user through the processes. The idea is that it leverages what ekoa has a lot, so it leverages knowledge, but it leverages the brand research. Brand research should be augmented to capture what it can about the company to pre-fill in this app the details about the company that it can capture. It should help the user and guide the user while providing support, with means to have all the documents in there.  The users should be able to select to have advice on what programs are available for him, or if they know where they want to go, they can go directly to the programs. We guide them in a visual way, like the other apps in Accor. They can do things by clicking and filling input fields, everything, or they can ask the assistant to do it. That should be suggested very often because this is a cumbersome process. It's better for them to use natural language talking to the assistant than filling out input boxes and pressing buttons.  The idea is that there's an area after they add what type of support, or after it creates a profile of the company. It asks a few questions about what the company is, what they could be looking for, and what they can benefit from, and then it uses the knowledge sources to figure out what is available.  Every time the user uses the app, or maybe nightly when he does the update of the index document, we could have a trigger event that the app listens to for specific sources. If a source was updated, then it will check for the profile of the company to see if it fits any new program with the dates for subscribing. It should notify the user, that kind of stuff.  But this app should not do that by default. That should be enabled when the user uses the app, because that will be expensive and the user has to make a conscious choice that he is going to use it.

notes.title: Fase 0: decisões
notes.body:
Gate de saída: tudo o que a Brasil Salomão possa querer fazer é suportado no novo. A BSM é o único cliente; quando o ERP funciona a 100% no novo, vai para produção. Decidir com muita segurança, mas decidir.

- Decisão: não envolver a Luciana nos testes pré-produção. Regressões novas podiam assustar e reabrir o ciclo de testes do lado deles. Fazemos tudo internamente; se escapar algum problema para produção, corrige-se e paciência. A decisão de ir para produção é nossa e tem de ser tomada com muita segurança.
- O drill (Garrison) é desejável para automatizar todos os testes do Ekoa no futuro, mas não é gate desta fase. Não deixar o perfecionismo do drill adiar a produção. (Acabar o drill "perfeito" é projeto do Garrison, não bloqueador do Ekoa.)
- Racional do gate: a BSM é o único cliente. "Suporta tudo o que a BSM quer fazer" é a definição operacional de "pronto".

notes.title: Citius / notariado
notes.body:
- Muito importante para advogados; parte do moat do vertical (com o Registo/audit trail). Deve existir, mesmo em v1 modesta, antes do anúncio do concurso, porque é argumento de adoção para o público-alvo.
- Citius: sem API pública conhecida; caminho provável é automação de browser com o certificado do advogado. Liga-se ao trabalho de automação já em curso no Garrison (campanha de testes de automação). Investigar antes de prometer âmbito.

notes.title: Fase 4: dependência do prémio
notes.body: O prémio do 1.º lugar do concurso inclui um Omi com a integração a funcionar. Esta fase tem de estar pronta antes do anúncio dos prémios.

notes.title: Bundles
notes.body:
Contexto: o programa de parceiros existe como documento e página, mas o Ekoa ainda não tem a funcionalidade de vender bundles. É pré-requisito do prémio de revenue share do concurso.

- Em aberto: mecânica exata do código de referral. Hipóteses faladas: pedir código no detalhe quando não há link; atribuir código ao parceiro apenas depois da primeira venda. Decidir quando se desenhar o checkout.
- Preços: a regra "nunca mostrar o preço do bundle sozinho" existe para o bundle nunca parecer um produto independente da subscrição.

notes.title: Contas gratuitas do concurso
notes.body:
- Unicidade garantida por SMS OTP: um número de telefone = uma conta gratuita. O mesmo mecanismo da votação.
- Limites falados: máximo ~50 prompts e teto de tokens. Números mencionados: 2M a 5M para a criação da app; 5M a 10M por conta na versão "experimentar o Ekoa". Decisão pendente do valor final. Recomendação: começar em 2M a 3M com possibilidade de top-up mediante pedido; um pedido de top-up é um sinal fortíssimo de lead interessada e uma oportunidade de conversa.
- O teto de tokens é o guardrail de custo real do concurso (ver n-custos).
- Auto-login por link: token de primeira sessão com expiração; mostrar também as credenciais para acesso posterior.
- Nota estratégica: isto é simultaneamente o funil de aquisição. Cada conta criada é uma pessoa com telefone verificado a experimentar o Ekoa de graça com limites. Não é preciso mexer quase nada no Cortex/Ekoa para além do SMS e da criação programática de contas.

notes.title: Desenho anti-fraude da votação
notes.body:
- Identidade de voto = número de telemóvel verificado por SMS. Um número, um voto. Este é o mecanismo principal; tudo o resto são camadas.
- Aceitar apenas números móveis portugueses (+351 9x). Bloquear números fixos e manter uma lista atualizável de prefixos/intervalos típicos de números virtuais (Twilio e afins). Aceita-se perder um ou dois votos legítimos com números estrangeiros: paciência.
- Racional de risco: o público (advogados) não é uma comunidade com perfil de ataque técnico; o custo de comprar números virtuais PT para escalar fraude é real e o ganho é pequeno.
- Correção técnica importante ao desenho inicial: "um voto por IP" não funciona em Portugal. As operadoras móveis usam CGNAT: centenas de utilizadores legítimos partilham o mesmo IP público. Um advogado a votar do telemóvel seria bloqueado pelo voto de outro. O IP e o fingerprint do browser não são identidade: são sinais e rate limiting. Concretamente: limitar pedidos de SMS por IP (ex.: 3 a 5 por hora, não 1 absoluto), limitar por número (reenvio com cooldown), captcha bom antes de qualquer envio de SMS, fingerprint como sinal soft para flagging.
- Email: pedir email único e filtrar domínios descartáveis é camada adicional válida para a conta/submissão, mas a unicidade do voto vem do telefone.
- Custos de SMS: ordem de grandeza 0,04 a 0,08 € por SMS em PT. Mesmo com 1.000 a 2.000 envios (votos + contas + reenvios), fica em dezenas de euros. O rate limiting é mais anti-abuso do que controlo de custo.
- Desempate: nunca por sorteio (arrasta o evento para o regime licenciado). Critério determinístico escrito no regulamento (ex.: em empate, decide a data/hora da submissão mais antiga, ou decisão fundamentada da organização).

notes.title: Prémios decididos
notes.body:
- 1.º lugar: conta Ekoa gratuita 3 anos + 20 horas de desenvolvimento para ajudar a desenvolver a própria aplicação (integrações, ligações a outros sistemas, partes complexas) + Omi com integração Ekoa a funcionar + entrada no programa de parceiros com link de venda.
- 2.º lugar: conta gratuita 2 anos + 10 horas de desenvolvimento + programa de parceiros com link.
- 3.º lugar: conta gratuita 1 ano + 5 horas de desenvolvimento + programa de parceiros com link.
- Revenue share igual para os três: 20% em vendas a clientes que já sejam Ekoa, através do link do vencedor; nas restantes vendas, aplicam-se as condições da página de parceiros. Os três ficam automaticamente inscritos no programa e recebem os links.
- O preço pretendido de venda da app é indicado pelo participante na submissão; não é final e está sujeito a aprovação do Ekoa.
- As horas de desenvolvimento são para a app premiada, com âmbito fechado por escrito antes de começar, agendadas em janela definida (proteção do tempo, que é o recurso mais escasso).
- Comunicação da conta gratuita: definir com precisão (nominativa, individual, não transmissível, limites de tokens do plano de referência). "Explicar bem, sem letra pequena escondida."
- Pendente: Omi só para o 1.º ou para os três primeiros. Recomendação: só o 1.º na primeira edição. Mantém o 1.º lugar distintivo (único prémio físico, boa fotografia de vencedor), controla custo e triplicar o suporte de integração na edição 1 é risco desnecessário. A escada já é generosa nos três lugares.

notes.title: Validações externas antes do anúncio
notes.body:
- A mudança de júri para votação comunitária mantém o concurso no campo do mérito (as pessoas votam na melhor aplicação; não há sorte em nenhum passo). A exclusão do regime das modalidades afins refere as operações que dependem exclusivamente da perícia ou mérito, dando o júri como exemplo ("nomeadamente... avaliados por um júri"). Votação pública por mérito é defensável, mas confirmar com o advogado que a exclusão se mantém sem júri, e manter a regra absoluta: nenhum elemento aleatório em nenhum ponto (nem desempates, nem brindes sorteados entre votantes).
- Imposto do Selo: o entendimento da AT afasta a sujeição quando não há fator sorte na avaliação. Confirmar com o contabilista que a votação comunitária preserva esse enquadramento, e o tratamento fiscal dos prémios em espécie (Omi) e das horas de desenvolvimento.
- Deontologia: comunicação centrada na solução construída, nunca na captação de clientes do premiado. Dados fictícios obrigatórios nas submissões, declaração assinada.
- Regulamento com RGPD (telefones e emails recolhidos), propriedade intelectual (participante mantém a app; licença de divulgação ao Ekoa), direitos de imagem, moderação/barra mínima de validade das submissões.

notes.title: Orçamento real do concurso
notes.body:
- A maior linha de custo não são os prémios: são os tokens das contas gratuitas. Conta rápida: 150 contas × teto 5M × consumo médio 40% ≈ 300M tokens; ao custo efetivo de agente de código, isto é entre várias centenas e poucos milhares de euros, conforme modelo e caching. Com teto de 10M e boa adesão, multiplica.
- Alavancas: teto inicial baixo (2M a 3M) com top-up a pedido; prompt caching agressivo (a proteção de margem de maior alavancagem, já identificada como subutilizada); modelo mais económico para estas contas se a qualidade aguentar.
- SMS: dezenas de euros. Omi: ~90 a 150 € por unidade. Troféu/selo se se mantiver: ~100 €.

notes.title: Registo de decisões do concurso (substitui secções do brief-premio-ekoa-advogados.md v0.1)
notes.body:
1. Júri eliminado. Motivos: difícil recrutar jurados com incentivo real; carga de avaliar muitas aplicações; e sobretudo o desenho pretendido é comunidade: pessoas descobrem num fórum, acham giro, criam a sua app, instalam e experimentam as apps das outras, e votam. O prémio principal é decidido por votação comunitária verificada (ver n-votacao). A "categoria do público separada" do brief anterior deixa de fazer sentido: o público é o mecanismo.
2. Prémios revistos conforme n-premios (3/2/1 anos, 20/10/5 horas, Omi, revenue share 20% + programa de parceiros). Cai a "subscrição vitalícia": passa a prazo definido. Cai o pacote imprensa/troféu como prémio central (pode manter-se como reconhecimento, decisão posterior).
3. Hardware decidido: Omi, condicionado à integração Ekoa pronta (Fase 4). MacBook e iPhone confirmados como fora.
4. Submissão simplificada: descrição + link da app no Ekoa + preço pretendido. O vídeo de 3 minutos do brief anterior cai (reduzir fricção); reavaliar se fizer falta para a galeria.
5. Calendário: deixa de ser fixo; passa a depender do roadmap (Fases 0 a 6 antes do anúncio). O princípio "anúncio só depois das férias judiciais e com 12 a 15 pré-comprometidos" mantém-se.
6. Mantém-se válido do brief anterior: todo o levantamento legal e fiscal (§5), a lógica de dados fictícios e sigilo (§5.4), o conteúdo mínimo do regulamento (§5.5) e o risco número um: o prémio vazio.

notes.title: Fora de âmbito enquanto este roadmap corre
notes.body:
- Decisão consciente de foco: enquanto este roadmap não chega ao fim, ficam pausados o Ekoa OS Run 1, a campanha de testes de automação (exceto o que alimentar diretamente Citius/Omi) e o site Visita v2. Não é abandono, é sequência. Registado aqui para ser uma escolha e não uma deriva.
- Motivação escrita pelo próprio: "estou sempre a ter ideias e nunca mais estou pronto para ter utilizadores a sério. Tenho de terminar isto, pôr a versão nova em produção e começar a ter utilizadores reais."

notes.title: Workflows, Notifications and Channels: brief (2026-09-03)
notes.body:
Source: the roadmap brief "Workflows, Notifications and Channels" (2026-09-03), merged here as one feature line. Placement: right after Fase 0 (deploy and testing priorities); this is the next major feature line once Fase 0 closes. Nothing was built for this entry. The product UI is PT-PT (wording is D9); this entry keeps the brief's English terms. Agent and workflow docs live in neutrally named files; no file is named after an AI vendor or assistant.

Thesis: Ekoa stops being a set of apps the lawyer operates and becomes a colleague that works ahead of the lawyer inside those apps, hands everything over as reviewable changes with evidence, and learns from corrections instead of prompts.

Principles every item must respect:
- Initiative: inbound events (a court notification, an email, a message, a document, a call) trigger work before anyone asks.
- Nothing lands as a fact: work lands as a proposal, a done-with-undo, or a question; the lawyer approves, edits, discards or reverts.
- Reversible by default, gated otherwise: autonomous changes happen only on reversible surfaces (Ekoa apps and Ekoa data); anything that leaves Ekoa passes a gate until the lawyer explicitly flips that gate to automatic.
- Progressive autonomy: every gate starts as "ask"; "always do this" makes it automatic for that workflow; every automatic gate can be flipped back.
- Corrections are the training mechanism: the lawyer never writes prompts; edits and rejections become standing instructions (lessons) for that workflow, the same mechanism integrations use.
- No empty screens: every screen shows what Ekoa already did or proposes on the lawyer's own data.
- Spend is visible and controllable: each workflow shows what it did in the lawyer's terms next to what it cost; everything proactive can be disabled with one tap; a global ceiling protects against surprise spend.
- Meet the lawyer where they already are: email and WhatsApp are first-class inbound and outbound channels; Ekoa is usable without opening Ekoa.
- Ekoa is the single place to act: the notifications area is complete enough that everything needing the lawyer's action is there.

Vocabulary (kept this small):
- Integration: anything that talks to a system outside Ekoa (API, CLI, MCP, browser steps); exposes Actions; holds credentials via the Cofre. Unchanged by this brief.
- Ekoa action: an automation of an Ekoa app through the built-in JavaScript mechanism, no browser; brought back as a first-class step type.
- Workflow: a linear list of steps with one trigger; replaces "automation" as the user-facing word for multi-system orchestration; no conditions, loops or diagrams; branching is expressed as separate workflows.
- Trigger: manual (press play), listener (an event happened), schedule (via the existing Schedules entity, D1).
- Step: integration action, Ekoa action, agent step, gate, notify.
- Run: one execution of a workflow; produces a summary, a change journal (for undo) and a cost record.
- Notification: proposal, question, done (with undo where available), alert.
- Channel: a communication surface connected to the tenant (email, WhatsApp, Slack, Teams, Discord), inbound and outbound.
- Package: what Ekoa sells and installs; now contains apps, artifacts, integrations and workflows; system workflows are the base set, like base artifacts.
- Base entities: a small sector-agnostic data model every user has (entities and processes with stable ids) that apps and workflows reference when present and extend with their own fields (D4).

Workflows (brief section 3):
- Entity: tenant-scoped, private by default, same sharing model as integrations (super admin publishes a frozen snapshot as global; enabling a global workflow creates a tenant copy; tenant edits never flow back). Fields: name, description, trigger, ordered steps, enabled flag, gate settings per gate, lessons (editable text per workflow), cost summary, last run evidence. Workflows hold no secrets. Exposed through the OpenAPI contract like integrations so every caller (chat agent, Garrison, external apps) inherits create/list/run/enable.
- Triggers: manual (play button on the workflow, in the chat, or via API); listener on the Cortex event bus (sources in scope: integration sync produced new items, first Caixa Citius; inbound email; inbound channel message; Ekoa data event such as document uploaded or record created/changed; a run of another workflow finished, which allows chaining without loops); schedule through the Schedules entity. Listener filter: an optional natural-language "when" clause evaluated by the model on the event payload, run on the cheapest tier and logged with its verdict. Two workflows on the same event with different filters replace an if node.
- Step types: integration action (calls an existing action through the integrations capability; inherits the write gate, self-heal and self-extension); Ekoa action (runs the built-in JavaScript automation against an Ekoa app and records before-images into the run's change journal); agent step (a natural-language instruction executed by the Ekoa agent with the tenant's full context; input is the event payload plus previous outputs; output is structured, text plus optional artifacts and proposed changes; follows the same reuse ladder as integrations, crystallising a repeated Ekoa operation into an Ekoa action); gate (pauses the run and asks the lawyer with a drafted payload and a small set of options: continue, continue with edits, stop, and "always", which flips the gate to automatic for this workflow; automatic gates still emit a done notification; gates are the only human-in-the-loop primitive); notify (emits a notification without pausing).
- Gate ergonomics (D7): when a draft is possible, present the drafted message directly with "send, edit, don't send, always send these" in one round trip; use the two-step form (choose an approach, then confirm the final text) only when the question is open. The loop must feel like pressing 2, not like a chat.
- Editor: reuse the steps editor that came from automations and now lives in integrations; a vertical list of steps with the trigger at the top; no conditions, loops, branches or canvas; each step shows evidence from the last run by type (screenshots for browser steps, example results for API actions, output for CLI actions, a change diff for Ekoa actions, the produced text for agent steps, the lawyer's answer for gates); per-step private feedback as in integrations; test run from the editor against a sample event.
- Reversibility and undo: every run writes a change journal (record id, before-image, after-image per Ekoa data change; documents edited by a run saved with tracked changes where the surface supports it, contract editor first). Undo per run reverts all journaled changes when no later change touched the same records; otherwise the conflict is shown as a diff for manual revert. External side effects cannot be undone and are therefore gated by default; the run summary always states them.
- Run summary: what came in, what was done, what is proposed, what needs an answer, what it cost; written for reading and for listening; becomes a notification delivered through the configured channels.
- Cost controls: token accounting per run, rolled up per workflow and per trigger kind (manual vs proactive), reusing the existing per-feature AI billing; a value receipt next to cost (notifications triaged, deadlines created, replies drafted, clients answered); enable/disable per workflow with one tap anywhere the workflow is shown; a global monthly ceiling for proactive runs (D2) that pauses proactive workflows and emits an alert while manual workflows keep working; model routing (filters, classification and identity resolution on the cheapest tier; drafting and agent steps on the strong tier) through the existing tiered router; on install only high-confidence, low-cost system workflows are enabled.
- System workflows and packages: packages carry workflows alongside apps, artifacts and integrations; a base set ships with the legal package, versioned, published as frozen snapshots; enabling one creates the tenant copy and asks only for the configuration it declares (which mailbox, which WhatsApp number, which Citius account), the same mechanism that drives onboarding; the tenant chooses when to take a new version.
- Creation UX: three entry points ("Automate something" on the Workflows page; the same button on the main conversation page; the in-conversation suggestion when the agent detects a repeatable request, the primary discovery path, which must be reliable before the buttons matter) leading to one conversational flow that asks what to automate, what usually happens and which systems are involved, drafts trigger and linear steps, shows them in the editor, runs a test and enables on confirmation; missing integrations are configured inline through the Cofre portal.
- Onboarding: replaced by the package installer conversation (about five minutes: what they usually do, which systems they use: Citius, bar email address, CRM, mailbox provider, WhatsApp, calendar); answers configure integrations and enable the matching system workflows; ends with the day-one reconstruction (catalog 14).

Notifications area (section 4):
- Entity: type (proposal, question, done, alert), status (pending, answered, archived), payload (text, draft, options), correlation (workflow, run, gate), delivery log, answer. Badge count in the app header equals pending items; done items auto-archive once read; alerts stay until acknowledged. Completeness principle: anything that needs the lawyer's action anywhere in Ekoa produces a notification.
- Delivery: always in-app; in addition to connected channels in a configurable preference order (WhatsApp first if connected, then Slack, Teams, Discord, then email); delivery text uses the run summary format; questions carry numbered options plus a free-text option.
- Reply routing: a reply on a channel (a number, a short text, an edited draft) is matched to the most recent pending question in that channel and recorded as the gate answer; ambiguous replies produce a clarifying message rather than a guess; the gate resumes the run immediately.
- Audio: every substantive notification delivered on a channel that supports audio also carries a text-to-speech version; per-channel toggle, on by default where cost allows (D3); reuse the voice work already in Ekoa and Garrison.

Channels (section 5):
- Inbound surfaces: a CC email address per tenant (optionally per user) to file documents, create tasks, add knowledge, ask for a draft or start a workflow; a dedicated Ekoa WhatsApp number per tenant (text, audio, images, documents); direct messages to the Ekoa app on Slack, Teams and Discord through the existing integrations.
- Media pipeline: audio transcription (reuse the existing transcription path); images OCR and vision description; documents parsed and extracted for every format that enters a matter, including scanned PDFs.
- Routing: a routing agent decides what an inbound item is and where it goes (knowledge base, a matter's files, a task, a draft reply, a new workflow, a question back to the lawyer, or a regular conversation turn), using tenant context to resolve matters and clients. Auto-ingest: a document that looks like knowledge or belongs to an identifiable matter is filed immediately with a done notification with undo; no confirmation step.
- Personal use: messaging the Ekoa number or CC address is a full conversation with the Ekoa agent, with the same context as the in-app chat; the path for capturing thoughts, voice notes and documents on the move.

Client and lead workflows (section 6):
- Positioning: standard system workflows on the channels clients already use (email and WhatsApp), not a separate assistant link.
- Identity: inbound sender resolved against Ekoa data by email or phone; known client routes to client workflows; unknown sender routes to lead workflows; ambiguous cases ask the lawyer once and remember the answer.
- Remit and disclosure: automated replies cover status of a matter, logistics, document collection and scheduling, never legal advice or opinions; anything outside the remit becomes a question to the lawyer with a drafted reply; status answers are composed only from approved facts (matter timeline and app data); every automated message states that it was prepared by the firm's automated assistant and whether the lawyer reviewed it (exact PT-PT text is D5); every exchange is written to the matter timeline.
- The loop: message arrives, identity and intent resolved on the cheap tier; agent step drafts the reply from approved facts; gate to the lawyer on their preferred channel (drafted reply plus "send, edit, don't send, always send these for this kind of request"); send with disclosure, log to the matter, done notification; "always" flips the gate and the lawyer receives done notifications only, reversible at any time.
- Sending identity (verify during discovery): email from the lawyer's own mailbox through the mailbox integration with the disclosure line; WhatsApp through a dedicated assistant number per tenant on the WhatsApp Business platform (constraints to verify in Phase 0); clients who keep writing to the lawyer's personal number are handled by the lawyer forwarding, never by connecting the personal number.
- Lead intake: acknowledge within minutes, ask the intake questions the lawyer would ask, run a conflict check against existing clients and counterparties, summarise to the lawyer with a proposed next step; informational only, no solicitation (Ordem dos Advogados publicity rules).

System workflow catalog (legal package, v1 targets; trigger, gate, default state, phase):
1. Citius notification triage: listener on Citius sync; classify; compute the deadline (Prazos); attach to the matter; draft the procedural response (Contratos) where applicable; draft the client message; create the calendar entry; gate before any client message or external write; default enabled; Phase 1. First proof of the whole model.
2. Document ingest: listener on inbound document (channel, CC email, upload); parse; route to knowledge or matter; done with undo; default enabled; Phase 2.
3. Voice debrief: listener on inbound audio from the lawyer; transcribe; extract facts, decisions, deadlines and follow-ups; update the matter; draft follow-ups; gate on outbound messages; default enabled when a channel is connected; Phase 2.
4. Morning brief per matter: schedule (weekday mornings); one paragraph per active matter on what changed, what is due, what Ekoa proposes; one message with audio; default enabled; Phase 3.
5. Client status reply: listener on inbound message from a known client; the loop above; in the catalog, enabled during onboarding when a client channel is configured; Phase 5.
6. Lead intake: listener on inbound message from an unknown sender; as above; catalog; Phase 5.
7. Deadline watch: schedule (daily); check upcoming deadlines against evidence of progress in the matter; alert with a proposed action; default enabled; Phase 3.
8. Contract review against firm templates: listener on contract opened or uploaded in Contratos; compare with the firm's templates and lessons; propose redlines as tracked changes; offer a plain-Portuguese client summary; no external effect, so no gate, proposal only; Phase 6.
9. Legislative change to client outreach: schedule (daily) over the indexed corpus (Diário da República, DGSI, DRE, ACT); detect new laws or acórdãos; match against client situations in the firm's matters; draft a short informational note per affected client; gate before sending; catalog, start with a narrow set of law areas; Phase 6.
10. Hearing recording transcription for appeals: manual on an uploaded recording; transcribe with timestamps; let the lawyer mark passages; produce the passage references and excerpts required for an appeal on matters of fact; Phase 6.
11. Adversarial rehearsal: manual on a pleading; play opposing counsel and the judge; return the strongest attacks and the acórdãos most likely to be used against the position, with sources; proposal only; Phase 6.
12. Client audio explanation: manual or from Contratos; plain-Portuguese explanation of a document; audio version; gate before sending to the client; Phase 6.
13. Quiet client reactivation: schedule (monthly); clients without contact in N months with open or recurring matters; draft an informational check-in; gate; catalog; Phase 6.
14. Day-one reconstruction: manual, run at the end of onboarding; from Citius and the mailbox, reconstruct matters, open deadlines and client contacts; present the practice picture; Phase 4.

Principles that are not workflows but must be in the roadmap (section 8):
- No empty screens: each app's main views show what Ekoa did or proposes on the lawyer's data (margin suggestions in Contratos, the change summary in a matter, the pending items in Caixa Citius); app views must be able to render proposals coming from runs.
- Matter as a concept, not a prerequisite entity: no shared matter entity is required before workflows start; an app that needs data checks whether the schema or object already exists for that user before creating new ones; workflows do not care how the data is obtained; if resolving "which process is this about" works differently on one user's data than on another's, the agent step adapts; apps remain, but they are also capabilities invoked in the context of a matter.
- Agnostic base entities: every user gets a small sector-agnostic base model (entities and processes with stable ids) that apps and workflows reference when present and extend with their own fields; the only shared structure, so Ekoa does not turn into a practice management system; shape and timing are D4.
- Firm brain: everything decided, drafted and corrected becomes institutional memory queryable by anyone in the firm ("how do we handle X here"); mostly the existing knowledge system plus lessons; needs the corrections from gates written into it.
- Corrections as standing instructions: edits at gates are summarised into the workflow's lessons and, when they concern style or tone, into tenant-level style memory used by every agent step.

Cross-tenant learning ledger (section 9): nightly aggregation of run metadata across tenants (workflow shape: trigger, step types, integrations used; outcome; gate decisions: ask, edit, stop, always; failures and self-heal events; duration; cost); fixed schema, metadata only (no payloads, document content, message bodies, client names or free text), enforced at the collector; used to improve system workflows, tune defaults and rank in-conversation suggestions; access limited to the super admin; documented on the security page in the same transparent style as the Cofre ("we learn from how workflows run, never from your content"); opt-out per tenant is D6.

Architectural rules for everything new (section 10):
- One engine: workflows use the existing runner and step executors; no second orchestration engine.
- Everything is a Cortex capability behind the OpenAPI contract with drift gates, so Garrison, external apps and the chat agent inherit it.
- Tenancy by user everywhere; no endpoint without a user; AI features billable.
- Secrets only in integrations via the Cofre; workflows, notifications and channels never see credential values.
- Event bus inside Cortex; listeners are subscriptions with optional model-evaluated filters; every event and verdict is logged.
- Channels are integrations too (they carry credentials and talk to outside systems); the notifications capability calls channel actions to deliver; the routing agent receives channel events through the bus.

Phasing: start after Fase 0 closes. Phases 1 and 2 are independent enough to run in parallel worktrees (D10); both depend on the notifications entity, built first inside Phase 1. The phases are the items of this line.

Non-goals: conditions, loops, branches or canvas editors in workflows; image or video generation; a separate client portal or assistant link; connecting the lawyer's personal WhatsApp number as a bot; any automated legal advice to clients; a second orchestration engine or a second automation concept alongside integrations.

notes.title: Workflows, Notifications and Channels: Phase 0 repo scan (2026-09-03)
notes.body:
Read-only scan of ekoa-code on 2026-09-03 (main at 3bd4493), done while merging the brief; nothing was built. Verdicts: exists = implemented and wired (routes mounted, schemas in shared/); partial = some pieces exist; new = nothing found. Where the code disagrees with the brief, the divergence is recorded here instead of adapting the brief silently. The adjacent repos (../ekoa-dev, ../ekoa-deploy) were not available in the session, so claims about them are unverified. Still open for Phase 0: the WhatsApp Business platform constraints (external check) and the D4 product decision.

Reuse map (brief section 10):
- Integrations capability, list/get/execute via OpenAPI: exists. docs/openapi/cortex.v1.json is generated from the shared/ descriptor maps with a drift test (api/tests/contract/openapi-drift.test.ts); routes in api/src/routes/integrations.ts under requireUserOrApiKey; api/src/integrations/integration-capability.ts; plus POST /api/v1/integrations/{key}/achieve (execute-or-author).
- Write gate: exists. api/src/integrations/action-consent.ts (approval keyed on org, user, integration, action, request shape and destination; once or always; 90-day TTL), enforced at the single executor api/src/integrations/action-executor.ts, so the capability route, the automation integration step, listener ticks and the agent tool all pass through it; approval and trust routes are auth user, so a gateway key can never self-approve.
- Lessons per integration: partial. api/src/integrations/definition-lessons.ts, routes, web/components/integrations/lessons-panel.tsx; read into prompts through the server-side load_context seam; the write is auth user (recorded deviation, 2026-08-03). Divergence: lessons are hand-typed only; a step correction writes a user-correction memory (api/src/automation/service.ts) and evicts the fingerprint cache, it does not feed lessons; shipped baseline packages have no lessons surface (the tenant forks first). The brief's "corrections become lessons" is new work on top of this.
- Sharing with frozen snapshots and tenant copies: partial. Tenant-scoped rows, visibility private/org/global, super-admin publish doors, and a frozen scrubbed publishedSnapshot read through crossOrgView (api/src/integrations/definition-store.ts, publish-scrub.ts, definition-registry.ts). Divergence: there is no copy-on-enable; enabling a global or shipped integration is a credential config row and the tenant keeps reading the frozen snapshot; a copy happens on first authoring (fork in integration-achieve.ts) or as a hidden recipe-overlay carrier row (D-RECIPE-OVERLAY, 2026-09-01). Re-publish is not tenant-opt-in: a new snapshot replaces the old one for every consumer at once. The brief's "enabling creates a tenant copy; the tenant chooses when to take a new version" would change this model.
- Per-step private feedback: exists. api/src/integrations/action-feedback-store.ts (org and user in the id), action-feedback.ts, ActionNotes in web/components/integrations/action-detail.tsx, isolation suite api/tests/security/action-feedback-isolation.test.ts.
- Steps UI with evidence by backing type: partial. A read-only vertical steps view with per-step screenshot evidence, backing labels (api-call, browser-steps, bash-cli), the learned-recipe panel and run history lives in web/components/integrations/action-detail.tsx over api/src/integrations/action-evidence-view.ts. Divergence: the steps EDITOR was deleted in convergence slice S8; web/app/(dashboard)/automations/* redirects to /integrations and the editor components under web/components/automations/ (step-list, step-card, step-forms, trigger-picker, integration-action-picker, result panels) are orphaned. The brief's "reuse the steps editor that now lives in integrations" is wrong as stated: what lives in integrations is a viewer; an editor is new work or a revival of the orphaned components.
- Automations runner (vision, steps, self-heal) as the browser backing type: exists. api/src/automation/engine.ts, vision through the llm chokepoint, rehearsal.ts, self-heal.ts, recipe.ts, replay-action.ts (zero-model replay), executors/injected-call.ts; an automationBinding resolves to backing type browser-steps (api/src/integrations/definitions.ts); self-extension is achieve (api/src/integrations/integration-achieve.ts). Backing types today: api-call, bash-cli, browser-steps, tenant-read. MCP does not exist (placeholder docblock only; backingType is a string on the wire, so adding one is additive).
- Ekoa actions: partial, and not what the brief describes. api/src/automation/executors/ekoa-action.ts plus platform-primitives.ts is a deterministic interpreter: it reads an artifact's MANIFEST.md capability recipe and walks typed primitives over appDataStore, no browser, no model. Divergence: it is not a JavaScript engine (no isolated-vm, quickjs, node:vm or eval anywhere in api/src); ekoa_action is an automation step type (api/src/automation/types.ts), not an integration action backing type; the self-heal fixer may not author it (decision 2026-08-03); its result panel is orphaned in web/. The chat agent already carries a call_ekoa_action tool seam (api/src/agents/tools.ts).
- Schedules entity: exists and merged on main (no feat/schedules branch remains; the code is in the tree). shared/src/schedules.ts: once and recurring (IANA timezone, DST-aware), target union manual | automation | integration_action, run statuses running/ok/failed/blocked/pending/done/dismissed, every endpoint user-or-key; api/src/schedules/{service,store,supervisor,recurrence}.ts; web/app/(dashboard)/schedules. The supervisor is a 30 s claim-first tick with MAX_CONCURRENT_FIRES 3 and a FAILURE_CEILING of 20 that auto-pauses (blocked runs are neutral, 2026-08-19). A workflow target would be a fourth additive kind (D1).
- Citius connector with completeness-verified sync: exists. api/src/legal/citius-sync.ts over api/src/events/verified-sync.ts (two-pass reconciliation; the watermark advances only on a proved complete outcome) with sync_state and sync_reports stores and events/sync-lessons.ts; suites api/tests/legal/citius-sync-completeness.e2e.test.ts, api/tests/security/citius-sync-metadata-only.test.ts, api/tests/contract/citius-sync.test.ts, api/tests/schedules/citius-reference-schedule.test.ts. Landed rows are metadata only in citius_notifications (operator lock: the sync never opens a document; document actions are separate, D-CITIUS-DOCUMENT-ACTIONS 2026-08-31). The citius package declares listenerConfig.pollAction consultar_notificacoes with the event notificacao.recebida, and legal-citius declares onNotificacaoCitius and onEmail handlers, so a landed item can already drive a trigger. Divergence: the sync route (api/src/routes/sync.ts) is dashboard-auth, flagged default-off and deliberately not a capability (2026-08-03).
- Cofre and bridge: exists. api/src/cofre (single policy seam unwrap() in service.ts; items, grants, sessions, session checkout, relay, audit), api/src/bridge (pairings, daemon WS, file delegation delegate_to_local, attended ceremonies, session and secret delivery), clients/bridge, COFRE_ENGINE_VERIFICATION.md, BRIDGE_VERIFICATION.md. Divergence for the rule "secrets only in integrations via the Cofre": user-defined integration credentials are still in a Rule-10 shadow (api/src/integrations/credential-cofre.ts: credentialsCiphertext remains the live read, cutover-or-remove review date 2026-08-15, only the origin binding is live from the Cofre), and the platform OAuth custody plane (platform-oauth.ts, m365-proxy.ts, pipedream.ts, app-sso-sessions.ts) never routes through unwrap(). The rule holds as intent, not yet as code.
- Knowledge system: exists. Org-partitioned markdown vault plus SQLite FTS5 lexical index (api/src/knowledge/vault.ts, index-store.ts), a reserved read-only _shared legal corpus, ingest by upload, the nightly crawler (api/src/knowledge/crawl, 03:00 local) and a build-scoped seam; search is user-or-key; chat tools knowledge_search and knowledge_read plus the cited-or-silent grounding block. Retrieval is lexical, not embeddings. No corrections or lessons are written into it today.
- Voice fitting and transcription path: partial. WS /api/voice/stream (STT relay) and WS /api/voice/tts-stream (TTS with barge-in) are wired (api/src/voice, shared/src/voice.ts) with a PT/EN TTS text pipeline (voice/text) and metering to usage_events. Divergence: only stub providers are registered (voice/stub-providers.ts: "v1 ships ONLY these; live vendors are C6, vendor-gated"); no Deepgram, Google or ElevenLabs SDK is a dependency; the vendors exist as config strings only (config.ts VoiceConfig, DEEPGRAM_API_KEY). The transcription path the brief wants to reuse does not reach a vendor yet. No realtime voice-to-voice.
- Tiered model router and per-feature AI billing: exists. api/src/llm/router.ts tiers FAST, WORKHORSE, EXPERT, GENIUS (models and weights in api/src/config.ts), a RouterDecision required at every call, completeFast() pins the cheapest tier, the classifier attribution kind is the cheap-call vocabulary; api/src/llm/attribution.ts feature keys (about 20 UserWorkAgentType values); single ledger writer api/src/billing/tracker.ts (token_events: billeeUserId, agentType, artifactId, sessionId, runId, tier, raw and metered tokens); monthly base allowance, hard limit default on, pre-run checkAllowance (402 BILLING_BLOCKED), billingLocked (402 BILLING_LOCKED), per-user, per-org and per-key sliding spend windows with a burn alert. Divergences relevant to 3.7: token_events carries no orgId (attribution is per user, feature and run, never per tenant); the breakdown endpoint and the web usage page are super-admin only; no per-run cost is stored on the run record (runId is on the ledger row, so it is derivable); the pre-run gate is called by interactive entries only, the schedules supervisor and the crawler never call it, there is no mid-run kill and no org-level budget object. A global proactive ceiling is new.
- Configurable assistant and chat modes through the Cortex API: partial. Modes (do, show, teach) exist for the served-app assistant only (shared/src/app-assistant.ts, header-scoped auth); the platform chat agent has no modes and its endpoints are auth user or token-query, so an external client cannot drive the chat with an API key. The chat agent does carry tool seams for the catalog, call_integration_action, call_ekoa_action and start automation (api/src/agents/tools.ts, agents/index.ts), plus knowledge, load_context, delegate_to_local and docx tools. The key-driven agentic surfaces are integrations achieve and the Anthropic-compatible gateway (api/src/llm/gateway.ts).
- Cortex event or webhook mechanisms: partial, and more than the brief expected. api/src/events is an inbound integration-event rail: persisted triggers (kind webhook or listener; listener is inferred server-side for providers without webhook ingress, 2026-08-14 and 2026-08-31), a durable event_queue, webhook_audit on every ingress, HMAC-verified POST and GET /hooks/:triggerId (api/src/routes/hooks.ts, with the Meta hub challenge), polled listeners (events/listener-supervisor.ts, integrations/event-sources/platform-poll.ts and user-defined-poll.ts), and exactly two delivery targets bound at the composition root: startAutomationRun and invokeArtifactBackend (events/delivery.ts). Event names are provider events declared by packages (citius/notificacao.recebida, imap/message.received, whatsapp/message.received, stripe and ifthenpay payments). Four in-process SSE streams (chat, job, automation, notifications) serve the dashboard. Divergences: no platform event vocabulary (no Ekoa data events and no run-finished event; sub_automation and the call_automation tool are synchronous invocation, not eventing); no model-evaluated filter anywhere (events/ imports nothing from llm/); no outbound webhook to external consumers.
- In-app notification mechanism: partial. shared/src/notifications.ts is one SSE endpoint (GET /api/v1/notifications/events) carrying the NotificationEvent union (build_intent, chat_answer, integration_build_intent, integration_ready, usage_updated, change_request, branding_updated, schedule_blocked, sheet_ready and similar), transient and per connection. The only persisted, unread-tracked notification row is per artifact (the notify.inApp RPC writing the app's own _notifications collection, api/src/apps/backend-runtime/handle-rpc.ts), and a bell with an unread count exists only inside the legal-pack artifact layouts. Divergence: no platform notifications entity, no inbox page, no acknowledge-required alerts, and no badge in web/components/header.tsx (it subscribes to usage_updated and branding_updated only); the one pending queue is change requests (settings/pedidos). The notifications entity of section 4 is new.
- Inbound email and WhatsApp handling: email partial, WhatsApp inbound exists. Email: connected-mailbox polling for Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace produces a frozen EmailInput (integrations/event-sources/email-hydrate.ts) dispatched to artifact backends that declare onEmail (dispatch-input.ts); the imap package is shipped but every call is refused as unsupported_transport (deferred). Divergence: there is no per-tenant CC or forwarding address and no inbound-email webhook provider; ingestion is poll-the-owner's-mailbox. WhatsApp: the shipped Meta Cloud API package (api/assets/integrations/whatsapp: send_message, send_template for outside the 24-hour window, mark_read, get_media_url; webhook with signature verification against the tenant's own app_secret and the hub challenge; event message.received) and a working inbound path (whatsapp-hydrate.ts, frozen MessageInput, wamid dedup, fan-out to backends; legal-nucleo's onMessage consumes it). Divergence: the number is the tenant's own Meta Business number entered as a credential; Ekoa provisions nothing (D8).
- Outbound email: partial. No platform mailer exists at all (no nodemailer, SendGrid, Resend or SES; no auth, invite or activation mail). Sending from the lawyer's own mailbox through the mailbox integration exists (shared/src/app-email.ts and api/src/integrations/app-email.ts: send, draft, draft/send, capability-based discovery, the owner's OAuth grant, consent gate), which is what 6.5 asks for.
- Slack, Teams, Discord, SMS: Slack partial (shipped package with a bot token, send_message and list_channels, outbound only, no webhook or listener config); Teams new (the microsoft-365 package is mail, files and profile only); Discord new; SMS new (roadmap f2 has not landed).

Brief sections 3 to 9, item by item:
- 3.1 Workflow entity: new. No entity named workflow exists; the closest is Automation (shared/src/automations.ts: Automation, Plan, PlanStep, RunRecord; nine step types including integration and sub_automation; triggers in shared/src/triggers.ts), whose /api/v1/automations contract is public and versioned (Rule 7) and must stay, while its user-facing surface was removed in slice S8. Divergence to settle at design time: today "automation" means per-site steps against one outside system and is being folded into Integrations by CONVERGENCE_PLAN.md (2026-08-17) and CORNERSTONE_PLAN.md (2026-08-28, mint-on-plan); the brief's workflow is cross-system linear orchestration with a trigger, so it is a new entity that reuses the engine rather than a rename. Reusable for the entity: tenant scoping, visibility, the publish snapshot (with the copy-on-enable and republish divergences above), the lessons and per-user feedback patterns.
- 3.2 Triggers: manual partial (automations and schedules have run-now; there is no workflow to run); listener partial (persisted triggers of kind listener and webhook with a durable queue exist for integration events; Ekoa data events, run-finished events and model-evaluated filters are new); schedule exists as an entity, the workflow target is new (D1).
- 3.3 Step types: integration action exists (the automation integration step already goes through the one executor with the write gate); Ekoa action partial (deterministic manifest-recipe interpreter, not JavaScript; no before-image capture); agent step partial (api/src/agents/authoring-core.ts authorWithRepair is a generic instruction-to-typed-draft executor shared by the integration agent and the planner, but there is no structured envelope of text plus artifacts plus proposed changes, and no job queue: jobs run in-process, FIXED-8); gate partial (action-consent once/always and the awaiting_consent, needs_credentials and pause_for_user halts exist; a drafted-payload question with continue, edit, stop and always, answerable from a channel, is new); notify partial (SSE push exists; a persisted notification is new).
- 3.4 Editor: partial. The read-only steps view with per-step evidence exists in integrations; the editor is orphaned (reuse map above); per-step private feedback exists; test run partial (the integration-builder test is HTTP-only with an arg map; there is no dry run against a sample event, and no dryRun, sampleEvent or previewRun anywhere).
- 3.5 Reversibility and undo: new for records. No before-image or after-image journal exists: the collections engine (api/src/data/collections-engine.ts) keeps only a _rev CAS and overwrites; Registo (shared/src/registo.ts) is metadata-only activity; api/src/apps/backups.ts is a whole-collection restore net; artifact source undo is git-based (api/src/apps/versions.ts). Tracked changes for documents exists (docs/word-track-changes.md, api/src/services/docx-redline.ts, apps/app-docx.ts, the docx tool specs). Divergence: "Contratos" is a docx generator from process data, not a rich contract editor; the redline capability sits in the services layer.
- 3.6 Run summary and notification: partial. RunRecord carries a summary, step records, consent and credential requests; run history and logs are on /api/v1/automations/runs; a summary in the lawyer's terms written for listening and turned into a notification is new.
- 3.7 Cost controls: partial (billing in the reuse map). Exists: attribution per feature and run, tiers, allowance and caps, billingLocked. New: per-run and per-workflow roll-up surfaced to the user, value receipts, the trigger-kind split, a global proactive ceiling that pauses listener and schedule runs, per-tenant attribution, gating of background work. Enable/disable: schedules have enabled and autoPausedAt and triggers have a disabled state; there is no org-level AI feature-flag map (settings expose pipedreamEnabled, verifyBuilds and memory.autoExtract).
- 3.8 System workflows and packages: partial. Three unrelated package notions exist: integration packages in api/assets/integrations (11 shipped: citius, slack, stripe, microsoft-365, imap, whatsapp, google-workspace, zoho-sign, adobe-acrobat-sign, invoicexpress, ifthenpay), content packages in api/src/content, and featured artifacts in api/assets/featured-artifacts (42, docs/featured-artifacts-ledger.md). Divergence: no single installable bundle spanning apps, artifacts and integrations, no install or enable-package flow, and nothing about workflows in packages. Configuration questions declared by a package exist for integrations (configSchema; D-INTEGRATION-CONFIG-CHANNEL, 2026-08-31).
- 3.9 Creation UX: partial. Conversational creation exists for integrations (chat marker to the builder panel, api/src/agents/integration-agent.ts) and for apps ([[EKOA_BUILD]]); free-text automation planning exists from the goal box on the Integrations page (web/components/integrations/automate-goal-box.tsx, POST /api/v1/automations/plan) and goes straight to rehearsal, not to an editor. In-conversation detection of repeatable requests is new (the only intent markers are build and integration build, api/src/agents/markers.ts).
- 3.10 Onboarding: partial. A guided onboarding chat session exists (web/components/chat/onboarding-card.tsx, onboarding-welcome.tsx, api/src/agents/guided-build.ts, web/e2e/onboarding.spec.ts, legal chips in web/lib/verticals/legal.ts); it asks what the user does, then proposes and builds an app. A package-installer conversation that configures integrations and enables workflows is new.
- 4.1 Notification entity: new (reuse map above).
- 4.2 Delivery: partial. In-app SSE push exists; channel delivery exists only as integration actions (whatsapp send_message and send_template, slack send_message, email through the owner's mailbox); the preference order, the delivery log and the notification-to-channel bridge are new.
- 4.3 Reply routing: new. No inbound message is correlated to a pending question; inbound WhatsApp and email terminate in artifact backends. Adjacent journaled refusal to design around: typed-OTP automation is refused (api/src/cofre/relay.ts, decision 2026-08-18, api/tests/automation/no-typed-otp.test.ts); a gate answer such as "2" is not an OTP, but the design must keep that line.
- 4.4 Audio: partial. The TTS text pipeline and WS surface exist with stub providers only; a vendor and per-channel audio delivery are new.
- 5.1 Inbound surfaces: CC email new; WhatsApp exists (on the tenant's own number); Slack DM new (outbound only today); Teams and Discord new.
- 5.2 Media pipeline: audio partial (stub STT); images partial (the chokepoint accepts images and app-vision extracts documents from photos; no generic OCR or describe-image in chat or knowledge ingest); documents partial (PDF text layer via api/src/services/pdf-text.ts with a deliberate no-OCR rule, tesseract rejected as a second egress path, scans routed to vision; DOCX via @adeu/core; knowledge upload indexes only markdown and text, other formats are stored as registered).
- 5.3 Routing agent and auto-ingest: new. The dispatch fork (integrations/event-sources/dispatch-input.ts) routes by source to artifact backends, not by content; knowledge ingest and matter filing from an inbound item are new.
- 5.4 Personal use: new. No channel reaches the platform chat agent; chat endpoints are dashboard-only.
- 6.2 Identity: exists as an app precedent, new as a platform capability. legal-nucleo's backend (api/assets/featured-artifacts/legal-nucleo/scaffold/backend/index.js) resolves email by case-insensitive equality and phone by exact digits or a unique 9-digit PT suffix against clientes, marks ambiguity as por-associar, and stores matchInfo provenance; legal-citius classifies sender provenance. Nothing in api/src does this.
- 6.3 Remit and disclosure: new. No disclosure wording exists anywhere (D5). Any user-facing privacy or custody claim lands under web/lib/privacy-claims.ts (CLAIMS_SHIP_GATED).
- 6.5 Sending identity: email exists (the owner's mailbox through app-email); WhatsApp partial (Business platform package with templates; a dedicated number per tenant is new, D8).
- 6.6 Lead intake and conflict check: new.
- 7 Catalog dependencies: Citius sync exists; Prazos, Contratos, Caixa Citius and Agenda exist as featured artifacts (legal-prazos, legal-contratos, legal-citius, legal-agenda) with deterministic engines in api/assets/legal-engines (prazo.mjs CPC/CIRE deadline math, citius-parser.mjs, agenda.mjs and others); Google Calendar actions exist in the google-workspace package; the legal corpus exists (api/assets/knowledge/sources.seed.json: dgsi, diario-republica, act-trabalho, dgert, pgdlisboa; api/src/legal/research.ts, cited-or-silent) as lexical search; hearing transcription has an API route (/api/legal/transcricao) but STT is stubbed; tracked-change redlines exist.
- 8 No empty screens: new (app views do not render proposals from runs; the served-app notify.inApp row is the nearest hook). Matter as a concept: partial. The legal spine (api/assets/legal-spine/contract.md and spine.mjs: clientes, processos, prazos, documentos, eventos, lancamentos, tarefas, with foreign keys) is a client-side convention over the generic owner-shared app_data store (api/src/data/collections-engine.ts, scope usr.<owner>), byte-copied into about 20 legal scaffolds; no matter, case or dossier type exists in shared/src or api/src/data. Divergence on "an app checks whether the schema or object already exists before creating": the check exists only as the legal pack's seed-only-when-empty rule (spine.mjs shouldSeed; legal-nucleo seeds, satellites read), and the app-builder persistence skill (api/assets/bases/app-auth-persistent/skills/using-persistence.md) teaches neither the shared namespace nor a reuse check, so the general claim is overstated. Base entities: new (the mechanism exists, no sector-agnostic model). Firm brain: partial (knowledge is org-queryable; corrections are not written into it). Style memory: new (memory has private/org visibility and a guardrail tier; org branding.toneOfVoice is used only in served-app brand prompts; the chat tone is static content).
- 9 Learning ledger: new. No nightly cross-tenant aggregation and no collector; the metadata-only Registo ledger (shared/src/registo.ts, super-admin cross-org read) and the super-admin grid (api/src/auth/capabilities.ts, 19 descriptors including the global integration review gate) are the anchors; docs/security.md already carries the transparent style to mirror (the Cofre custody split, the anonymisation scope note), but there is no security page in web/. Garrison note: Garrison is an ordinary external API client of Cortex and must stay one; scripts/garrison-grep.sh (npm run gate:garrison, FIXED-7) fails the build on any Garrison import or service call in api/src or shared/src.

Divergences that change the brief's assumptions, in one list:
1. Ekoa actions are a deterministic manifest-recipe interpreter, not a JavaScript engine.
2. The steps editor no longer exists; integrations hold a read-only steps viewer; the editor components are orphaned.
3. Sharing has no copy-on-enable, and republish is not tenant-opt-in.
4. Corrections feed a memory, not lessons; shipped packages have no lessons surface.
5. "Automation" is live as a public contract and engine and is being folded into Integrations (convergence and cornerstone plans); "workflow" must be a new entity that reuses the engine, and D9 interacts with that removal (the current UI term is "Automatizações", not "Automações").
6. Voice has stub providers only; no transcription vendor is wired.
7. Billing is per user, not per tenant; background work is not gated by the allowance; no per-run cost on the run record.
8. The notifications rail is transient SSE; nothing is persisted at platform level.
9. Inbound email is mailbox polling with no CC address; WhatsApp runs on the tenant's own number.
10. Credentials are not yet only in the Cofre (a shadow with an overdue review date; the OAuth custody plane sits outside unwrap()).
11. No matter entity; the legal spine is a scaffold convention; the general "apps check before creating" claim is overstated.
12. MCP backing type, Teams, Discord and SMS do not exist.

Key files to cite: api/src/routes/integrations.ts; api/src/integrations/{definition-store,action-consent,integration-achieve,definitions,definition-lessons,app-email}.ts; api/src/integrations/event-sources/{dispatch-input,whatsapp-hydrate,email-hydrate}.ts; api/src/automation/{types,engine,recipe,replay-action,self-heal}.ts and executors/ekoa-action.ts; api/src/events/{service,delivery,verified-sync,listener-supervisor}.ts; api/src/legal/citius-sync.ts; shared/src/{integrations,automations,triggers,schedules,events,notifications,registo,billing}.ts; docs/openapi/cortex.v1.json; api/src/llm/{attribution,router}.ts; api/src/billing/{tracker,allowance,rate-caps}.ts; api/src/voice/{providers,stub-providers}.ts; api/src/agents/{tools,index,authoring-core,markers}.ts; api/src/data/collections-engine.ts; api/assets/legal-spine/contract.md; api/src/apps/backend-runtime/handle-rpc.ts; api/src/cofre/{service,relay}.ts; api/src/integrations/credential-cofre.ts; web/components/integrations/action-detail.tsx; web/components/header.tsx; web/locales/pt.ts; web/lib/privacy-claims.ts; docs/security.md; docs/decisions.md (2026-08-03 CS4/CS6 and lessons entries, 2026-08-17 schedules, 2026-08-18 typed-OTP refusal, 2026-08-28 cornerstone, 2026-08-31 listener inference, 2026-09-01 D-RECIPE-OVERLAY); CONVERGENCE_PLAN.md; CORNERSTONE_PLAN.md.

notes.title: Workflows, Notifications and Channels: open decisions (owner Gonçalo)
notes.body:
Status: all pending. Owner: Gonçalo. Copied from section 12 of the brief (2026-09-03). Each carries the brief's recommendation where one was given; the repo scan (see the Phase 0 note) adds what the code already fixes.

- D1. Schedule as a third trigger kind through the existing Schedules entity, versus keeping schedules separate. Recommendation: extend Schedules with a workflow target. Scan: the Schedules entity on main is one entity with an additively widened target union (manual, automation, integration_action; decision of 2026-08-17), so a workflow target is the shape the entity was designed for.
- D2. Default global monthly ceiling for proactive runs, and whether it is per tenant or per user.
- D3. Audio on notifications on by default, and which TTS tier for routine messages versus substantive ones.
- D4. Whether a shared matter/client entity exists across the legal apps; if not, whether to build it before Phase 1 or alongside it. Scan result recorded in the Phase 0 note.
- D5. Exact PT-PT disclosure text for automated client messages, in two variants (reviewed by the lawyer, sent automatically).
- D6. Tenant opt-out for the learning ledger, and how it is presented.
- D7. Gate ergonomics: adopt the one-step form (drafted message plus four options) as default, keeping the two-step form for open questions.
- D8. Whether the WhatsApp channel launches with a dedicated assistant number per tenant (recommended) or waits for a way to use the lawyer's own number.
- D9. UI vocabulary in PT-PT: "Fluxos" versus "Automações" for workflows; wording for gates ("Aprovar", "Sempre"), notifications and channels. Scan: the dashboard already uses "Automações", "Integrações" and "Agendamentos" in web/locales/pt.ts, and the convergence plan (CONVERGENCE_PLAN.md) is removing the automation-branded surface in favour of Integrations, so the choice interacts with that plan.
- D10. Order of Phases 1 and 2: sequential or parallel worktrees.
